steps.what: Attend professional meetings, educational conferences and teacher training workshops

tasks.design: Keep participation and learning with the teacher. Materials in {LMS} can support attendance without replacing practice, discussion or reflection.
tasks.previous_blocker: Competence develops through engagement with content and peers.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing digital materials support learning but earn no new labour saving.
tasks.still_hard: Turning general guidance into suitable classroom practice.
tasks.human_edge: Reflecting on experience and testing new methods with professional care.
tasks.altitude: No change to learning time or professional responsibility.

reach.learn: Evaluate the relevance of training evidence

evidence.claim: Attendance and professional learning remain human activities; no documented saving is established here.

assumptions: Boundary is attending and engaging, not booking events or recording certificates.
No structured-input consumer or new capture requirement is introduced.
Native learning-material access is sufficient; no build is proposed.
Zero upkeep because the existing professional-learning process continues.
research_questions: Which training activities lead to useful changes in classroom practice?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, gross0 and net0 after zero upkeep. Reading a generated summary is not counted as equivalent attendance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Participate in staff meetings and committees

steps.what: Read staff meeting agendas and committee papers to prepare a contribution
Attend staff meetings and serve on committees through discussion and agreed actions

tasks.design: Keep agendas and papers accessible in {DOCS}. Retain the teacher's preparation, discussion and committee contribution; the task does not establish a separate minutes-writing baseline.
tasks.previous_blocker: Committee service requires informed representation and agreement with colleagues.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing shared papers support participation without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Reconciling different classroom priorities and school constraints.
tasks.human_edge: Representing pupils' needs and negotiating workable decisions.
tasks.altitude: Committee responsibility and participation time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Clear decision questions and action ownership

evidence.claim: No documented capability in the digest removes substantive staff participation or committee judgement.

assumptions: Boundary is teacher preparation and participation, not chairing, minute taking or calendar administration unless separately assigned.
No new structured agenda or decision-log producer is required by an automated action.
Use native shared-document access before considering custom tools.
Zero upkeep because no new meeting mechanism is introduced.
research_questions: Are meetings delayed by unclear decision questions rather than the teacher's participation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, net0 after zero upkeep. No preparation or attendance is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select classroom equipment, materials and supplies suitable for the children
Inventory classroom supplies and check equipment condition before replenishment
Order the checked supplies within delegated purchasing limits
Store equipment safely and issue materials to the classroom

tasks.design: Use native favourites and requisition forms in {PROCUREMENT} for repeat classroom orders. The teacher still selects suitable materials, counts and checks stock, approves the exact request and physically stores and distributes supplies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated ordering fields add effort to a mostly physical and educational task.
tasks.enabler_now: Native purchasing forms can reuse approved item references without inferring stock levels.
tasks.still_hard: Child suitability, damaged equipment and differing pack sizes.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing safe and useful materials for this group of children.
tasks.altitude: Less repetitive order entry; selection and handling responsibilities remain.

evidence.claim: Reusable purchasing forms are a model-knowledge proposal; the digest establishes no classroom-supply automation saving.

assumptions: Boundary includes teacher selection, count, requisition and handling; supplier fulfilment and purchasing-team processing stay outside the focal denominator.

Teacher produces item reference, count, condition, required quantity and unit in s2; all25 hours include stock capture. Teacher verifies recipient location and budget in s3, within its retained10 hours. No free par level or shortage flag is assumed.
Unknown items or pack conversions use manual entry and review in s3. Item catalogue upkeep is counted separately.
Test native favourites before custom code. A request above delegation goes to existing purchasing approval, not automatic supplier ordering.
unknowns: Native catalogue coverage and stock accuracy
research_questions: Do repeat order forms save time after quantity and pack checks?

approvals.approved_version: Exact requisition with items, quantities, units, budget and destination; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R90 gives gross10 minus upkeep3 = net7. Low assumes pack checks leave only3 hours entry benefit; high requires half the20-hour ordering step removed. Selection, inventory and physical handling stay unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Perform assigned library, hall, cafeteria or bus supervision duties and assist children

tasks.design: Keep supervision and physical assistance with the teacher. Duty assignments may be visible in {CALENDAR}, but calendar availability does not reduce attention or safe bus assistance.
tasks.previous_blocker: The work requires physical presence and immediate response to children.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology changes those physical duties in this design.
tasks.still_hard: Unpredictable movement, distress and competing supervision needs.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a child needing help and intervening promptly.
tasks.altitude: No change to supervision time or accountability.

evidence.claim: Physical school supervision remains unchanged; no labour saving is claimed from a digital roster.

assumptions: Library, hall, cafeteria and bus duties are alternative assignments, not a mandatory sequential chain. Boundary excludes making the duty roster.
No machine action consumes a structured child-presence or safety flag.
Native roster access is sufficient; no build is proposed.
Zero upkeep because supervision practices and tools remain unchanged.
research_questions: Where do pupil-transition handovers need clearer human responsibility?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 yields net0 after zero upkeep. No reduction in physical attention or assistance.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Kindergarten teachers retain learning, committee and pupil-supervision work; routine supply ordering may need less entry.
reach: Coordinate safe transitions with support workers and catalogue details with purchasing staff
role.ambitious_version: Reliable classroom support with practical purchasing improvements and full human attention to young children.
